SEC sues crypto lender Nimbus, alleging $1.2 billion fraud

Published 2026-10-06 15:40 UTC

The Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday sued crypto lender Nimbus Lending and its CEO Mark Ellery, alleging the firm defrauded more than 90,000 retail investors out of $1.2 billion.

According to the SEC, Nimbus marketed its Yield Vault product as a safe way to earn up to 14% a year by lending crypto to institutions, but it paid earlier investors with deposits from newer ones. The complaint also alleges Ellery took more than $40 million for himself.

Nimbus froze withdrawals in August. A lawyer for Ellery said he would fight the charges. The case is one of the largest crypto enforcement actions brought by the SEC this year, and bitcoin slipped about 2% after the news.

The SEC says Nimbus told investors their deposits would be lent only to vetted institutional borrowers with collateral, but instead moved about $400 million to a trading firm controlled by Ellery. When crypto prices fell, the trading firm lost much of that money, and Nimbus froze withdrawals for about 90,000 customers.

Nimbus marketed its interest-bearing accounts heavily through social media and podcasts, promising yields of up to 12% a year. The SEC alleges those accounts were securities that should have been registered, and that the company misrepresented both the risks and its own financial health in public statements.

The agency is seeking disgorgement of ill-gotten gains, civil penalties and an order barring Ellery from serving as an officer or director of a public company. Lawyers for Ellery said he denies the allegations and intends to fight the case in court.

The case is another sign that regulators are continuing to pursue crypto lenders that collapsed during the market downturn. Analysts said the outcome could shape how courts treat yield-bearing crypto products, and that customers hoping to recover their money face a long wait as the bankruptcy and the SEC lawsuit proceed in parallel.
